item.title: Flydubai pilot investigated over possible attempt to crash Tel Aviv-bound flight
item.description:
Relations between two countries soured in January when a UAE-backed force was defeated by Saudis Saudi Arabia is being urged to reconcile with the United Arab Emirates over Yemen as the price Riyadh must pay to form a military alliance capable of driving the Houthis back. Relations between the UAE and Saudi Arabia in Yemen, where both had backed anti-Houthi forces, plummeted in January this year when a force with which the UAE had been aligned – the separatist Southern Transitional Council (STC) – was attacked and defeated by Saudi Arabia in a move intended to squash its attempt to recreate a separate southern state. The UAE subsequently in effect quit Yemen. Continue reading...

item.title: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri named Morocco's first woman PM
item.description:
The king of Morocco on Tuesday named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri the country's first woman prime minister after her centre-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) party won last week's parliamentary elections. El Mansouri joined the PAM in 2008 and was also the first woman to serve as mayor of Marrakesh, winning the office in 2009 before losing it six years later, then retaking it again in 2021.

item.title: ‘Economic war’: Is Iran losing its leverage over the Strait of Hormuz?
item.description:
The biggest breakthrough yet in the Saudi-UAE rift came in a bland statement about “brotherly bilateral relations and regional developments.” UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed’s meeting with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh is the most prominent effort to repair ties, which have ruptured over competing interests in Yemen, Sudan, and elsewhere. Tuesday’s “ fraternal visit ” signals that intra-Gulf rivalries are taking a back seat as the US-Iran war threatens trillions of dollars invested in transforming the region’s economies. The UAE delegation included the heads of its national security council, crisis management authority, and defense procurement body, highlighting the focus on security. item.title: Iraq celebrates National Sovereignty Day as US troops withdraw
item.description:
A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight jihadists concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country's leaders, but which some fear will embolden pro-Iran armed factions. France 24's Angela Diffley takes a look at the security challenges facing the country and why the US has chosen this moment to take its troops out.

item.title: The October 7 warnings threatening Netanyahu’s Israeli election campaign
item.description:
The Israeli prime minister’s remarks at the UN weren’t just motivated by personal animosity In a boastful and defiant speech to the United Nations on Thursday, Benjamin Netanyahu called out a list of villains he insisted are intent on destroying Israel and promoting an anti-Jewish conspiracy by accusing Israel of committing a genocide in Gaza. He singled out the leaders of Hamas, Iran, Qatar and Turkey, among others. But Netanyahu spent considerable time on the global stage attacking an unusual target: Zohran Mamdani, the mayor of New York City. item.title: As AI political deepfakes go viral, lawmakers struggle to keep up – 2 states’ laws show limits of what they can do
item.description:
A woman views a manipulated video in January 2019 that changes what is said by President Donald Trump and former President Barack Obama, illustrating how deepfake technology can deceive viewers. Robe LeverAFP via Getty Images Imagine watching a political campaign video in which a candidate admits to taking a bribe. You recognize the face and voice. But the confession is entirely fabricated, thanks to artificial intelligence. Now imagine that your state has passed a law against these AI-generated election deepfakes . Would that mean the video has to be removed from the airwaves? In its June 2026 report, the National Conference of State Legislatures counted 31 states with election deepfake laws . item.title: FBI hunting the hackers who stole its employees' sensitive data
item.description:
The hackers behind the massive FBI breach told 404 Media on Monday they do not intend to publish the data. The breach, in which the hackers stole personal information on “all FBI employees and applicants” including physical addresses, job roles, names of spouses, and medical records, represents a significant national security and counterintelligence threat. Criminals in the same ecosystem as the hacking group, called ShinyHunters, have previously used hacked phone data to track and harass the FBI agents investigating them. When 404 Media first broke news of the breach, the group sent the personal data of an agent and their spouse who they said was investigating the group. Although any potential damage will be less if ShinyHunters doesn’t publish the data publicly, the theft happening at all still presents much of those same national security risks, with the data providing granular…

item.title: ‘Oozing everyman charm’: what the papers say about Andy Burnham’s speech
item.description:
The UK’s prime minister raised the specter of the country rejoining the EU , an issue that remains politically divisive despite growing numbers of voters voicing frustration over the lasting impacts of Brexit . Were Andy Burnham to support a campaign to reenter the bloc, he would draw a significant dividing line between his Labour Party and rival Reform UK, which, helmed by Brexit champion Nigel Farage, is neck-and-neck with Labour in polls. Such a move may be particularly tough because of its implications for immigration: “Any attempt to move closer,” a leading journalist wrote for the conservative Spectator magazine, “is unthinkable without throwing open the borders again … To put it mildly, this is not what the British public wants .” — Prashant Rao

item.title: WNBA playoffs: No 8 Liberty spring historic upset to take down No 1 seed Lynx
item.description:
New York are first No 8 seed to beat first seed Liberty ease to 2-0 series victory over Minnesota Jonquel Jones had 21 points and 13 rebounds and the No 8 seed New York Liberty beat the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx 87-71 in Game 2 of their WNBA playoff series on Tuesday night to advance to the semi-finals. Breanna Stewart added 21 points and Sabrina Ionescu had 18 to help the Liberty become the first No 8 seed to eliminate a No 1 seed in the league’s 30-year history. The WNBA has undergone a number of different playoff formats, and in many of them, it wasn’t possible for those seeds to match up. However, in 2022 the league changed to the current iteration in which the top-eight teams play in the quarter-finals. Continue reading...
